Please embed a watermark first on the Embed / Extract page
Ready. Select an algorithm and tap "Embed Watermark into Video".
Embedding finished: %1$d frames processed, watermarked video generated
Extraction finished: %1$d frames decoded for voting

"【Principle】Digital watermarking hides identification data in the video luminance component and must satisfy imperceptibility, robustness and security (Ch. 8, 8.1). The MP4/H.264 file is demuxed and decoded into YUV frames (Ch. 7 file formats, Ch. 6 coding standards), the watermark is embedded frame by frame in the luminance plane Y, then the stream is re-encoded with H.264 and remuxed into MP4.\n【Pipeline】Generate a 64×64 binary watermark G → embed per frame (LSB or DCT) → blind extraction with inter-frame majority voting.\n【Evaluation】Higher PSNR means better imperceptibility; NC closer to 1 and lower BER mean better robustness."

"【Principle】Spatial-domain LSB: replace the least significant bit of each cover pixel with a watermark bit (Ch. 8, 8.2); the change is at most ±1 and visually imperceptible.
【Eq. 8-1】cw = 2·⌊c/2⌋ + w, i.e. clear the LSB and write the watermark bit w∈{0,1}.
【Implementation】The 64×64 bit pattern is tiled over the whole luminance plane by modulo addressing (intra-frame redundancy); extraction counts occurrences per bit and takes a majority vote.
【Characteristics】Large capacity and low complexity; fragile to noise/compression, so robustness relies on intra-frame + inter-frame voting."

"【Principle】Transform-domain DCT: embed the watermark into mid-frequency coefficients of 8×8 DCT blocks (DCT is the core transform of JPEG/H.264, see Ch. 5; low-frequency changes are visible and high-frequency coefficients are discarded by quantization, so mid-frequency balances invisibility and robustness).
【Eq. 8-3】F′(u,v) = F(u,v) + α·pn(u,v)·(2w−1)
 where α is the embedding strength (30 here) and pn is a key-driven pseudo-random spread-spectrum sequence, w∈{0,1}.
【Extraction】Correlation despreading: w′=1 if Σ F′·pn > 0, otherwise w′=0.
【Characteristics】Strong resistance to JPEG compression; inter-frame voting further improves robustness."

Output/decoded frames: %5$d / %6$d"

"【Attack】Lossy JPEG compression (quality Q=10): coarse DCT quantization discards high-frequency detail (Ch. 5).\n【Effect】Watermark energy is attenuated by quantization; NC drops and BER rises.\n【Countermeasures】① Embed in DCT low/mid-frequency coefficients consistent with compression; ② increase embedding strength α; ③ spread-spectrum modulation; ④ inter-frame redundancy + majority voting (implemented here)."

"【Attack】Additive white Gaussian noise (σ=15): random perturbation on all pixels.\n【Effect】Many LSB bits flip; SNR of DCT coefficients drops.\n【Countermeasures】① Intra-frame tiling + inter-frame majority voting (implemented here); ② higher embedding strength; ③ transform-domain embedding exploiting DCT energy compaction; ④ low-pass pre-filtering before extraction."

"【Attack】Salt-and-pepper noise (density 5%): pixels forced to 0 or 255 with probability p.\n【Effect】LSBs of contaminated pixels are fully random.\n【Countermeasures】① 3×3 median filtering before extraction to remove impulse noise; ② majority voting; ③ skip pixels near extreme values when embedding."

"【Attack】3×3 mean filtering (low-pass): attenuates high-frequency content and LSB perturbations.\n【Effect】LSB watermark is badly damaged; DCT watermark is relatively stable.\n【Countermeasures】① Embed in low/mid-frequency bands; ② increase embedding strength α; ③ inter-frame majority voting; ④ prefer transform-domain embedding."

"【Attack】3×3 median filtering: ranks neighborhood values, removing impulse outliers but reordering LSBs.\n【Countermeasures】① Transform-domain watermark (coefficient ordering is more stable); ② redundant voting; ③ apply identical pre-processing at embedding and extraction (synchronized filtering)."

"【Attack】0.5× downscaling: destroys spatial synchronization (embedded positions shift).\n【Effect】Blind-extraction correlation drops sharply for both LSB and DCT.\n【Countermeasures】① Embed a synchronization template/reference to estimate the scale factor before inverse mapping; ② embed in a scale-invariant feature domain; ③ tiled redundancy reduces position sensitivity."

"【Attack】2° small-angle rotation with resampling: global pixel coordinate shift.\n【Effect】Geometric synchronization is broken; NC drops significantly.\n【Countermeasures】① Embed rotation-invariant quantities (Fourier–Mellin domain); ② estimate the rotation angle via a synchronization template and invert it; ③ embed in annular/polar regions."

"【Attack】10% border cropping: watermark information near the border is directly removed.\n【Effect】Some watermark bits are permanently lost; the center region survives.\n【Countermeasures】① Tiled redundant embedding — the watermark covers every full frame, so local cropping only loses local bits (implemented here); ② inter-frame majority voting compensates from uncropped frames; ③ concentrate embedding near the center."

"【Attack】Drop all odd frames (50% loss): a temporal-axis attack specific to video.\n【Effect】Temporal synchronization is broken; extraction still works when every frame carries the watermark.\n【Countermeasures】① Inter-frame redundancy — the watermark is embedded independently in each frame (implemented here); ② temporal synchronization codes to locate dropped frames; ③ adapt embedding strength to the frame-loss rate."
